source.title: Convergent World Representations and Divergent Tasks

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures representational alignment with CKA in a controlled synthetic setting, testing whether task diversity produces convergence rather than reproducing the broad scale, architecture, and modality comparisons in the claim.
record.gate_note: Rows cover reported CKA results on alignment across tasks, task counts, layers, and seeds. Fine-tuning results about integrating Atlantis cities concern adaptation and generalization, not alignment between models, so they are not rows here. CKA results available only in figures are not transcribed as unreported numbers; the rows use the authors’ textual descriptions where provided.
record.test_reason: Controlled synthetic test of the Multitask Scaling Hypothesis, a proposed PRH mechanism. Small Qwen2 transformers are trained from scratch on 1, 2 or 3 of 7 geometric tasks over one city world. CKA is measured between models with disjoint task sets, across layers 3–6, and across 3 seeds. It does not vary model scale, architecture or modality, and uses no natural data.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors also argue that convergence is driven by task diversity rather than data quantity or performance, since single-task models reach comparable accuracy. They note that a full PRH test would need cross-architecture comparisons, which they did not run.
record.recipe_differences: Uses synthetic geometric tasks on one shared city-coordinate world and small Qwen2 Transformers; measures CKA across task combinations, layers, and seeds. It does not compare models across architectures, modalities, or scale.
record.method_sensitivity: CKA varies across tasks and layers; crossing is near-zero when trained alone, while distance is less aligned with other tasks. The task-count trend also differs by layer: layers 4–6 saturate while layer 3 continues improving.

fits_no_version.finding: Single-task CKA partially predicts cross-task fine-tuning generalization of new entities; divergent tasks (distance) harm integration of new entities.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Representational divergence of a task in isolation predicts poor propagation of fine-tuning updates even after convergent multi-task pretraining.

record.code_released: https://cfpark00.github.io/world-rep-research-flow/ (the paper states that code, data, and analysis results are openly available)
record.problems: The study uses small-scale models, one architecture, one modality, and a synthetic setting. It measures alignment with CKA rather than checking other similarity measures. Some reported CKA values are presented in figures, and the prose does not give their exact values or SEMs.
record.rows_left_out: No additional convergence results left out. Fine-tuning and Atlantis integration results in Sections 5 and Appendix E.4–E.5 were excluded because they measure entity adaptation and task generalization, not convergence between model representations.

untested.parts: Model size/capability scaling, different architectures, natural data, and modalities; only task count is varied.
All; no vision-language or paired data.
Individual units/bases and specific feature recurrence; only CKA is measured.
All; no mapping, stitching or relative representations.
All; no interpretable feature or circuit comparison.
Alternative similarity measures, neighbour settings, and out-of-distribution inputs for convergence.
Separating a shared world/data source from a common model of reality, since all tasks share one world.

missing.what: Choice of task prefix used to extract representations has negligible effect on city representations (an input-choice robustness check)
Within-combination CKA across seeds increases with task count (1 to 3 tasks)
Single-seed aggregate over all non-overlapping pairs (105 two-task pairs, 70 three-task pairs) showing CKA rising with task count
Control: single-task models reach comparable task accuracy, so authors attribute alignment to task diversity rather than performance or data quantity

record.verdict_notes: Most CKA values are only in figures; the text gives exact numbers only for 0.84, 0.48, 0.89 and about 0.85. All models share one architecture and one world, so 'different objectives' here means different geometric tasks over identical latent data. The wider-model experiment reports only fine-tuning results, not CKA.

versions.untested_parts: Tests increasing task count as a proposed convergence mechanism, but not increasing model size or capability as such, different architectures, natural datasets, or different modalities.
No vision-language models or paired images and captions.
Measures CKA across seeds, not whether particular features or shared subspaces recur, nor whether individual units or bases differ.
No mapping, stitching, relative-representation, or unpaired alignment test.
No comparison of interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits.
Shows variation by layer and task condition using CKA, but does not compare alternative similarity measures, neighbour settings, or out-of-distribution inputs for convergence.

Does not establish whether shared training data or objectives, rather than a common model of reality, cause the alignment; all tasks use the same underlying world. Does not test convergence across large natural models.

conditions.value: layer 5 in main text; layers 3–6 in appendix

rows.subject: single-task models (aggregate across tasks)
rows.value: CKA values increase from layer 3 to layers 4–6.
rows.uncertainty: Mean ± SEM across 3 seeds is reported for the appendix CKA matrices; exact SEM values not stated in the prose.
rows.note: Aggregate layer trend across the single-task CKA matrices.

rows.subject: two-task models (aggregate across disjoint task pairs)
rows.operation_detail: Measured CKA between models trained on two-task combinations.
rows.baseline: Single-task models; values as low as 0.48 are stated for comparison.
rows.value: All off-diagonal two-task CKA entries exceed 0.84.
rows.uncertainty: Mean ± SEM across 3 seeds is reported; exact SEM values not stated in the prose.
rows.note: Aggregate across two-task model pairs. The authors state that alignment is higher even for models whose task pairs have no tasks in common.
rows.check: Observed for V1 along the task-diversity axis only. For V7, models sharing no objective still reach CKA >0.84, which argues against shared objectives as the cause. A shared world/data source remains, so shared data cannot be separated from a common model of reality.

source_check.correct: All off-diagonal two-task CKA entries exceed 0.84; single-task comparisons reach as low as 0.48. V1 state=cannot_determine because parameter size is fixed. The disjoint-task comparison does not isolate the causal explanation in V7: models retain a shared world and autoregressive objective.
source_check.locator_found: Section 4, Result 3; Appendix E.3, Two-Task CKA, Figure 12; Appendix C.3.
source_check.problem: The observed alignment does not directly establish size scaling or exclude shared training causes.

tranche.reason: Controlled synthetic experiments test representational convergence and the proposed multitask mechanism using a different experimental method.

source_check.notes: Representation analyses exclude Atlantis and city IDs beginning with zero. The reproducibility statement says all seeds were 42, despite repeated descriptions of three-seed CKA experiments; this internal inconsistency remains unresolved.

statements.correction: Fixed model architecture and size; task counts 1, 2, 3; disjoint comparison task sets; layers 4–6 plateau near 0.85 CKA at two and three tasks.
statements.problem: The saturation result is accurate, but it qualifies task-diversity scaling rather than directly limiting convergence with increasing model size.

statements.correction: Linear CKA used throughout; layers 3–6 show multitask convergence; layers 4–6 saturate near 0.85 while layer 3 continues improving; no alternative-metric or evaluation-dataset comparison in these results.
statements.problem: The cross-layer finding is accurate, but persistence across layers does not test robustness to the alternative metrics or evaluation inputs named by V6.

statements.correction: Disjoint geometric task sets retain high alignment; all off-diagonal two-task CKA entries exceed 0.84; shared city world, architecture, and autoregressive objective remain.
statements.problem: Disjoint geometric tasks are correctly described, but the result does not establish that shared objectives cannot account for alignment: all models use autoregressive training on the same underlying world.
